name: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
alt: East India Company rule in India

predecessors.name: Nawabs of Bengal
predecessors.text: the land within the Maratha Ditch and 600 yards beyond it and 'the zamindari of all the land between Calcutta and the sea', granted by Mir Jafar's treaty of 4 June 1757

successors.name: British Raj
successors.text: British India under the Crown from 1 November 1858, with the same vassal states

ledger.x: 23 March 1757: Clive and Watson take Chandernagore, three months before the Company's Plassey.
1757: after Plassey the Company holds the Calcutta zamindari.
June 1757: Bengal becomes a British puppet state.
15 January 1761: Pondichery falls to the British.
1762: Bombay is carried by this row from here.
1763: the British occupy Serampore.
1763: the British leave Serampore after the year the page gives; no month.
1763: Chandernagore is restored.
25 June 1765: Pondichery is handed back (first occupation, 15 January 1761 - 25 June 1765).
16 August 1765: the puppet nawabdom ends in the Company's diwani.
16 August 1765: the Company becomes revenue sovereign of Bengal and Bihar.
16 August 1765: Awadh is returned but made dependent.
1 March 1768: the Nizam cedes the Northern Circars to the Company.
29 March 1769: the Treaty of Madras gives Karur to Mysore.
1772-73: the Company drives the Bhutanese out of Cooch Behar.
25 April 1774: Bhutan makes peace.
1775: the sovereignty of Benares passes from Awadh to the Company.
1 March 1776: the Treaty of Purandar leaves Salsette to the Company.
1778: the second British occupation of Pondichery begins ('Second British occupation, 1778 - 1783'); no month.
1778: Masulipatnam leaves english-colonial-empire's shape.
1779: the English Colonial Empire row ends with Madras, which this row draws from 1780.
15 February 1779: Goddard captures Ahmedabad.
1780: small coastal additions in the south.
17 May 1782: the Treaty of Salbai ends the war; the Marathas 'agreed to return the territories it had captured from the British' and the British those they had occupied.
1783: the second occupation of Pondichery ends (1778 - 1783).
1783: three coastal cells dropped.
1784: the Bengal Duars go back to Bhutan.
1788: the Guntur circar passes to the Company.
1789: the Bengal Presidency settles the Andamans.
1791: Cochin becomes a semi-protected state under the Company.
18 March 1792: Tipu cedes half of Mysore to the allies.
23 August 1793: the third British occupation of Pondichery begins ('Third British occupation, 23 August 1793 - 18 June 1802').
1794: the British retake Chandernagore ('retaken by the British in 1794 in the Napoleonic Wars').
1794: an inland strip behind the Andhra coast enters the shape.
1795: Travancore comes under British protection ('Jaipur (1794) & Travancore (1795) come under British protection').
May 1796: the settlement is abandoned.
1798: the Nizam of Hyderabad signs the first subsidiary alliance ('Nizam of Hyderabad becomes first State to sign Subsidiary alliance introduced by Wellesley (1798)').
1798: the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War begins ('Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1798-1799)').
1799: Seringapatam falls and Tipu Sultan is killed ('Siege of Seringapatam, 1799').
1799: Mysore is carved up.
1799: Mysore becomes a Company protectorate.
1799: the administration of Thanjavur passes to the Company.
1800: the 1800 shape grows beyond the Mysore core (Karnataka +276 is the restored Mysore, drawn here as the vassal above).
1800: the Nizam cedes the Ceded Districts to the Company.
1801: the British occupy Dansborg (Tranquebar), with Balasore and Frederiksnagore: the page has them 'occupied Dansborg, Balasore and Frederiksnagore from 1801 to 1802'.
1801: the British occupy Frederiksnagore (Serampore); the page gives no day.
1801: Oudh cedes Rohilkhand, Gorakhpur and part of the Doab.
26 July 1801: the Nawab of the Carnatic signs the Carnatic Treaty.
1802: the first British occupation of Frederiksnagore ends ('from 1801 to 1802'); no day.
18 June 1802: the third occupation of Pondichery ends (Treaty of Amiens).
August 1802: Tranquebar returns to Denmark (a footnote on Danish_India quotes a letter of Serfoji II: 'on the 17th August A.
December 1802: the Treaty of Bassein.
August 1803: the fourth British occupation of Pondichery begins ('Fourth British occupation, August 1803 - 26 September 1816').
8 August 1803: the Second Anglo-Maratha War opens with the taking of the Ahmednagar pettah ('8 August 1803 - 24 December 1805').
September 1803: Lake beats Scindia at Delhi.
17 December 1803: the Treaty of Deogaon gives the Company Cuttack.
17 December 1803: the Treaty of Deogaon cedes southern Berar.
30 December 1803: the Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon.
1804: southern Berar passes to the Nizam.
8 October 1804: Holkar marches on Delhi.
1805: part of Bundelkhand is annexed ('parts of Bundelkhand annexed from Maratha Empire (1805)'); the page also lists 'Ceded and Conquered Provinces established (1805)'.
1805: Gwalior and Gohad are restored to Scindia.
1805: Baroda becomes a protectorate of the Company.
24 December 1805: the war ends with the Treaty of Rajghat, in which Holkar 'gave up Tonk, Rampura, and Bundi'; the page does not say who received them, so no gain is recorded.
24 December 1805: Holkar signs the Treaty of Rajghat.
24 December 1805: Holkar gives up Tonk, Rampura and Bundi.
1806: Sambalpur passes to the British.
1808: the British occupy Frederiksnagore a second time ('and again, from 1808 to 1815'); no month.
February 1808: Tranquebar is occupied again.
25 April 1809: the Treaty of Amritsar fixes the Sutlej.
1814: a belt of central India enters the shape.
1 November 1814: Britain declares war on Nepal ('1 November 1814 to 4 March 1816').
1815: the second British occupation of Frederiksnagore ends ('from 1808 to 1815'); no day.
1815: the Cis-Sutlej states ('Cis-Sutlej states (1815)').
20 September 1815: Tranquebar is handed back.
25 December 1815: Anjar comes under British occupation.
1816: Chandernagore returns to France ('The city was returned to France in 1816, along with a 3 sq mi (7.8 km2) enclave').
4 March 1816: the Treaty of Sugauli is ratified.
4 March 1816: the war ends with the ratified treaty; the British set up a Resident at Kathmandu.
26 September 1816: Pondichery is handed back ('Fourth British occupation, August 1803 - 26 September 1816'); the page has the five establishments returned to France in 1816.
1817: the states of Rajputana accept British suzerainty ('States of Rajputana accept British suzerainty (1817)').
13 June 1817: the Treaty of Poona.
5 November 1817: the Third Anglo-Maratha War begins ('5 November 1817 - 9 April 1819').
November 1817: the Bhonsle's troops attack at Sitabuldi.
21 December 1817: the British beat Holkar at Mahidpur.
1818: Jaipur enters the subsidiary alliance with the Company.
1818: Cutch accepts British suzerainty ('Cutch accepts British suzerainty (1818)').
1818: Scindia cedes Ajmer.
6 January 1818: the Treaty of Mandeswar (Battle_of_Mahidpur calls it the Treaty of Mandsaur).
1818: the Holkars lose land.
9 January 1818: the Nagpur treaty.
6 January 1818: the Treaty of Mandeswar.
9 January 1818: the Bhonsle treaty.
January 1818: the Saugor and Nerbudda Territories are formed from the northern Bhonsle lands and the Peshwa's Bundelkhand.
3 June 1818: 'BajiRao II surrendered to the British'; the Peshwa's subsidiary status ends in annexation.
3 June 1818: the Peshwa's state is annexed.
9 April 1819: the last fort, Asirgarh, falls and the war ends.
25 December 1822: Anjar reverts to Cutch.
1824: a 46-cell step.
11 May 1824: the British enter Rangoon in the First Anglo-Burmese War (formal outbreak 5 March 1824).
11 May 1824: the British enter Rangoon.

24 February 1826: the war ends at Yandabo, but 'Until the second installment was paid, the British would not leave Yangon' and the page speaks of 'the Rangoon area which were occupied for several years to guarantee compliance'; it gives no evacuation date, so the occupation is ended with the war as burma /ledger/11…
24 February 1826: the Treaty of Yandabo.
24 February 1826: the war ends at Yandabo; British troops stay at Rangoon until the second indemnity instalment.
1831: the protectorate becomes direct administration: 'Mysore State goes under British administration (1831-81)'.
1831: British administration of Mysore begins; the Wadiyar is not deposed, so the land is hatched, not annexed.
1833: Bahawalpur accepts British suzerainty ('Bahawalpur accepts British Suzerainty (1833)').
1834: Coorg is annexed ('Coorg annexed (1834)').
1834: Manipur, Arunachal and Nagaland cells enter the shape.
15 March 1835: the Jaintia kingdom is annexed.
1838: 'the British representative had the Amirs sign a political residency treaty'; a later treaty let British troops be stationed permanently in Sindh at the Amirs' cost.
1839: Aden is captured ('Aden is captured by Company (1839)').
13 November 1839: the British storm Kalat.
1841: the Assam Duars are annexed.
1841: the occupation ends.
1843: the Talpur tint ends in annexation (next event).
1843: Sindh is annexed.
17 February 1843: Napier's army invades Sindh ('invaded Sindh on 17 February').
24 March 1843: Napier marches out of Hyderabad against Sher Mohammad, the last action the page dates; the infobox runs 17 February-24 March 1843.
December 1843: Gough's army crosses the Chambal.
29 December 1843: Maharajpore and Punniar are fought.
1844: Chanderi District is ceded.
1845: Tranquebar is sold to Britain.
1845: the First Anglo-Sikh War begins ('First Anglo-Sikh War (1845-1846)').
11 October 1845: Serampore is sold to Britain.
1846: the Treaty of Lahore ends the First Anglo-Sikh War.
1846: a central-India belt enters the shape.
1846: under the Treaty of Lahore 'Sikhs cede Jullundur Doab, Hazara, and Kashmir to the British'.
9 March 1846: the Treaty of Lahore cedes Kashmir, Hazara and the hill country.
16 March 1846: the Treaty of Amritsar sells Kashmir to Gulab Singh.
1846: Kashmir is sold to Gulab Singh of Jammu ('Sale of Kashmir to Gulab Singh of Jammu under Treaty of Amritsar (1846)').
1848: Satara is annexed ('Annexation of Satara (1848)'; the Third Anglo-Maratha War page agrees: annexed 'under the doctrine of lapse' in 1848).
1848: the Second Anglo-Sikh War begins ('Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848-1849)').
1849: the Second Anglo-Sikh War ends.
1849: the Punjab is annexed ('Annexation of Punjab and North-West Frontier Province (1849-56)').
1849: Sambalpur is annexed ('Jaipur and Sambalpur (1849)').
1852: the Second Anglo-Burmese War begins ('Second Anglo-Burmese War (1852-53)').
1853: Lower Burma is annexed ('Annexation of Lower Burma'); the page gives the war as 1852-53, hence confidence 2.
1853: the Second Anglo-Burmese War ends.
1853: the Company applies the doctrine of lapse to Jhansi but does not take it.
1853: Berar is assigned to the Company.
1854: the Nagpur tint ends in annexation.
1854: Nagpur is annexed ('Nagpur and Jhansi (1854)').
1856: the Oudh tint ends in annexation.
1856: Oudh is annexed: 'With the annexation of Oudh in 1856, this territory was extended.'
4 and 10 December 1856: the British take Kharg Island and Bushehr.
10 May 1857: the sepoys of Meerut rise and the rebellion begins.
11 May 1857: the rebels reach Delhi and proclaim Bahadur Shah Zafar.
June 1857: British authority in Oudh collapses.
June 1857: the Kanpur sepoys rebel under Nana Sahib and besiege the British entrenchment.
Mid-July 1857: Kanpur is 'retaken by mid-July 1857'.
September 1857: Delhi is retaken 'by the end of September', the siege ending on 21 September.
October 1857: the British leave Bushehr.
19 November 1857: the Residency enclave at Lucknow is evacuated.
1858: the islands are taken again.
21 March 1858: Campbell's force clears the rebels out of Lucknow (it had evacuated the enclave on 18 November 1857).
5 April 1858: the fort of Jhansi falls.
5 April 1858: the contest over Jhansi ends with the fall of the fort.
June 1858: Gwalior is retaken.
17 June 1858: Gwalior goes back to Scindia.
1858: Chanderi is granted to Scindia.
1858: the Awadh countryside is regained, bridged at the end of the contest.
20 June 1858: the rebellion is contained with the defeat at Gwalior; hostilities were not formally declared over until 8 July 1859.

wars.name: Battle of Plassey and the conquest of Bengal
wars.outcome: British victory on 23 June 1757; Mir Jafar made Nawab and Bengal a British puppet state.

wars.name: Battle of Buxar and the Treaty of Allahabad
wars.outcome: Buxar on 22 October 1764; the Treaty of Allahabad of 16 August 1765 gave the Company the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, returned Awadh to Shuja-ud-Daula minus Allahabad and Kora, and left Awadh dependent.

wars.name: First Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Hyder Ali nearly captured Madras; the Treaty of Madras of 29 March 1769 'restored the status quo ante bellum, except for Mysore's acquisition of Karur' and pledged mutual defence.

wars.name: First Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Salbai (17 May 1782): both sides returned the territory captured in the war; Salsette stayed with the Company from the Treaty of Purandhar (1 March 1776), which 'annulled that of Surat' but, on the page, left the British the revenues of Salsette and…

wars.name: Second Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Mangalore of 11 March 1784 restored the conquests on both sides (Dindigul and Karur to Tipu Sultan, Mount Dilly and the Calicut factory to the Company); no territory was ceded.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Seringapatam, 18 March 1792: about one half of Mysorean territory divided among the allies.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Seringapatam falls in 1799 and Tipu Sultan is killed; much of Mysore is annexed by the British, the Nizam and the Marathas and the core restored to Krishnaraja Wadiyar III as a Company protectorate.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: British victory (8 August 1803-24 December 1805): Cuttack from the Bhonsle (Deogaon, 17 December 1803), Haryana, the Doab, Delhi-Agra, parts of Bundelkhand, Broach and Ahmednagar from Scindia (Surji-Anjangaon, 30 December 1803); Holkar gave up Tonk, Rampura…

wars.name: Anglo-Nepalese War
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Sugauli (ratified 4 March 1816): Nepal lost Kumaon, Garhwal, the Western Terai and all Sikkim; the Mahakali became its western and the Mechi its eastern boundary; a British Resident was set up at Kathmandu.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: British victory (5 November 1817-9 April 1819): the Peshwa surrendered on 3 June 1818 and his territories were absorbed into the Bombay Presidency; the Saugor and Nerbudda Territories were formed; Holkar became subsidiary; Rajputana accepted British…

wars.name: First Anglo-Burmese War
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Yandabo of 24 February 1826: Burma cedes Assam, Arakan and Tenasserim, loses influence in Cachar and Jaintia and pays one million pounds.

wars.name: First Anglo-Afghan War
wars.outcome: 'The British forces left Afghanistan after recovering prisoners' and Dost Mohammad 'was released and re-established his authority in Kabul' (First_Anglo-Afghan_War, paraphrased: the page names no territorial result).

wars.name: British conquest of Sindh
wars.outcome: British victory, 17 February-24 March 1843 (Miani, Hyderabad): 'Annexation of Sindh into the Bombay Presidency within British India'.

wars.name: First Anglo-Sikh War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Lahore (1846): 'Sikhs cede Jullundur Doab, Hazara, and Kashmir to the British'; Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh of Jammu (Treaty of Amritsar).

wars.name: Second Anglo-Sikh War
wars.outcome: British victory; the Punjab and the North-West Frontier Province were annexed (1849-56 on the page).

wars.name: Second Anglo-Burmese War
wars.outcome: British victory; annexation of Lower Burma.

wars.name: Indian Rebellion of 1857
wars.outcome: British victory (10 May 1857-20 June 1858): Delhi retaken in September 1857, Lucknow on 21 March 1858, Jhansi in March and Gwalior in June 1858; the Company was dissolved by the Government of India Act 2 August 1858.

certainty.note: Company land is a scatter of districts, factories and client states; inland frontiers with the Marathas, Mysore and Awadh are approximate and Cliopatria's cells are coarse.
Treaty and annexation borders: Sugauli (Mahakali and Mechi, 1816), Yandabo (1826), Sindh (1843), the Punjab (1849) and Lower Burma (1853) are fixed by treaty or annexation.
